name: Texture (ASDisplayNode, ASCollectionNode)
baseline: Auto Layout and manual frame layout of UICollectionView cells on the main thread
verdict_reason: Texture says it moves layout and text sizing off the main thread. In an independent 2025 benchmark its main-thread layout time for 100 cells is 5.4x-5.9x lower than Auto Layout and about half that of manual frame code. The comparison counts main-thread time only, which is the quantity Texture claims to reduce.
tier_reason: Public LayoutFrameworkBenchmark app run by a third party (layoutBox) with device, iOS version and Release mode stated; Texture's own README gives no numbers.
claimed_speedup: Main-thread time, 100 cells: iPhone 16 0.011 s (Texture 3.1) vs 0.0595 s Auto Layout (5.4x, derived from page data) and 0.0208 s manual layout (1.9x, derived from page data); iPhone 13 Pro iOS 18.6 0.0109 s (Texture 3.2) vs 0.064 s Auto Layout (5.9x, derived from page data) and 0.0216 s manual (2.0x, derived from page data).
workload: Same feed cell built as an ASCellNode in an ASCollectionNode; benchmark times vc.view.layoutIfNeeded() on the main thread for 10 to 100 cells.
os: iOS 18.6 (iPhone 13 Pro); iPhone 16 OS not stated
toolchain: Release mode per LayoutFrameworkBenchmark README; exact Swift and Xcode version not stated
one_liner: Node-based UI framework (ex-AsyncDisplayKit) that cut main-thread cell layout time 5.4x vs Auto Layout in an independent 2025 run.
how_it_is_fast: Texture's nodes are thread-safe wrappers around views and layers, so measurement, text sizing, image decoding and layout run on background queues. ASCollectionNode prepares cell nodes ahead of display, leaving the main thread to commit finished frames.
use_it_when: Long, image- and text-heavy feeds where main-thread layout and text measurement cause dropped frames
Teams able to adopt a whole parallel view hierarchy (nodes) for those screens
skip_it_when: SwiftUI apps or small screens where UIKit is already fast enough
Teams that cannot absorb a large Objective-C++ dependency and its node API
caveats: The benchmark times only main-thread work inside layoutIfNeeded(); Texture measures cell nodes on background queues, so part of its total CPU cost falls outside the timed window.
Texture's own README gives no numbers.
GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION; the LICENSE file states that all code is under the Apache License 2.0.
Single synthetic feed cell; visual output differs slightly between frameworks per the benchmark README.
tradeoffs: Large dependency with its own node hierarchy, layout specs and threading rules.
Total CPU work is moved, not removed; background layout competes with other background tasks.

evidence.quote: Texture lets you move image decoding, text sizing and rendering, layout, and other expensive UI operations off the main thread, to keep the main thread available to respond to user interaction.
